text: The rule-catalog read answers packageCode, packageVersion, versionState, inForce, ruleId, ruleVersion, actionText, ownerRole, timerSpec, toState, droolsRuleName and outputs for one rule in one package version, and the latest-state-change read answers entryId, ruleId, ruleVersion, decidedAt and missing in 200 whatever the case holds. An unknown rule row or version label is 404 with MSG-P3-027 for the rule row or version check, an absent or malformed parameter is 422 with MSG-GEN-001, and a store that cannot be read is 503 with MSG-GEN-006.
why: The two shapes are declared only from the consuming side and the TSD lists neither operation, so the field set, the empty answer and the two refusals HAVE to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them open would stop the story and every caller.

text: The latest state change of a case is the newest decision_log_entry row of that case, in chain_seq descending order, whose DF-DEC-004 rule_id and DF-DEC-005 rule_version are both present; no decision code list is read to make the choice, and an entry with neither is skipped rather than answered.
why: LOV-DECISION is named in the TSD and never enumerated, so a code list would be invented; the rule ID and the rule version are the two facts the fill needs and both are required fields of the entry.

text: A timer spec is returned as one string, character for character, and holds no meaning for this service: the caller parses 'n working days', 'n days' with a label, 'same day', 'immediate', 'next working day', 'None', 'payment due 30 days' and 'deadline driven', and applies the service levels and timers table where it needs one. No due date, no working-day count and no holiday is computed in rwb-decision.
why: The column has no list and two legacy values fit neither of the legacy four shapes, so the only safe default is to hand the string back unchanged; any parsing here would put a business duration in the registry.

text: packageVersion is required on the catalogue read. A call without it is refused 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, and this service never answers from the version in force when the caller names none, because an action already set must be read under the version that set it.
why: The published path leaves the value empty and the legacy rule forbids a later version rewriting an action already set, so a default would break BR2 and BR10 of the legacy key; the refusal is the only answer that keeps both.

why: The WP fixes the two metadata rows and the rules make only H blocking, so the DP-added platform and consumed contracts must be recorded as defaults rather than as blockers; otherwise the lane would be cut and the story re-dated.
